target.title: fix(workshop): keep approval target names UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary
- Keep Skill Workshop lifecycle approval target skill names UTF-16 safe when the approval description is length-bounded.
- Add a regression through `proposeCreateSkill` and `resolveSkillWorkshopToolApproval` so the proposal filesystem state and approval resolver path are both exercised.

## What Problem This Solves
Skill Workshop lifecycle approvals include a bounded `Target skill:` line. The old formatter used `requestedSkillName.slice(0, Math.max(0, availableSkillNameLength - 1))`, so a long proposal name with an emoji or other astral character at the truncation boundary could put a lone UTF-16 surrogate into the approval description.

Latest `origin/main` still has the raw slice at `src/skills/workshop/policy.ts`:

```text
origin/main=d5fb4903f1b13a4309d479f1011d995b1fc706ae
95:      : `${requestedSkillName.slice(0, Math.max(0, availableSkillNameLength - 1))}…`;
```

## User Impact
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Operators reviewing a Skill Workshop apply/reject/quarantine approval should see a valid target skill name. Long Unicode skill names should be shortened cleanly rather than rendering a replacement character or malformed half-surrogate in the approval prompt.

## Origin / follow-up
Follows #102816.

- Follows: #102816 fixed the same UTF-16-safe truncation class for gateway command-list strings by replacing raw length clamping with `truncateUtf16Safe`.
- Gap: Skill Workshop lifecycle approval descriptions still used raw code-unit slicing for the target skill name.
- Consistency: This applies the shared UTF-16-safe truncation helper at the source approval-description formatter without changing approval policy, proposal lookup, or lifecycle actions.

## Competition / linked PR analysis
- Related open PR scan: checked open PRs for `workshop skill approval target UTF-16` in `openclaw/openclaw` before submission.

```json
[]
```

No open same-point PR was found.

## Merge risk
- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility, automation, availability, security-boundary, session-state.
- **Risk explanation:** The relevant surface is approval prompt formatting for Skill Workshop lifecycle actions. The patch does not change whether approval is required, which decisions are allowed, how proposals are loaded, how skill content is applied, or any persisted proposal schema. It only changes the truncation helper for an overlong display field.
- **Why acceptable:** The diff is limited to one formatter line and one resolver-path regression. Existing control-character sanitization, max approval description length, timeout behavior, and lifecycle policy remain unchanged.
- **Patch quality notes:** Focused source change plus a regression that creates a real pending proposal on disk and resolves the exported approval policy. No skip/only directives, no type escapes, no fallback/default strategy, and no unrelated cleanup.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High: latest main still has the raw slice, no same-point open PR was found, the patch uses the repository's existing UTF-16-safe helper, and the regression covers the proposal-to-approval path.

## Real behavior proof
- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A Skill Workshop proposal whose long target skill name has an emoji straddling the approval truncation boundary should produce a valid `Target skill: ...…` line without a lone surrogate.
- **Canonical reachability path:** user/config/input → schema/type/ingestion/normalization → runtime object → request/effect: user skill proposal input (`name`, `description`, `content`) enters `proposeCreateSkill`, is normalized into a pending proposal record and written to the workspace proposal store, is resolved by `resolvePendingSkillProposal` during `resolveSkillWorkshopToolApproval`, becomes lifecycle approval runtime data, then renders the bounded `requireApproval.description` effect shown to the operator.
- **Boundary crossed:** The regression creates an actual temporary workspace proposal via `proposeCreateSkill`, reads it back through `resolveSkillWorkshopToolApproval`, and observes the exported plugin approval result rather than calling the private formatter directly.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** The fix uses the existing shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. No provider-owned external constraint is involved; the relevant repository constraint is `PLUGIN_APPROVAL_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH`, which remains enforced.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux local worktree, Node/Vitest, temporary workspace directories and Skill Workshop proposal files via existing test utilities.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
source /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-followup-102816-evidence/context.env
cd "$TASK_WORKTREE"
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
...
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 15.01s
```

```text
origin/main=d5fb4903f1b13a4309d479f1011d995b1fc706ae
95:      : `${requestedSkillName.slice(0, Math.max(0, availableSkillNameLength - 1))}…`;
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The regression constructs the proposal name so the emoji starts exactly where the old raw slice would keep only the high surrogate. The resolved approval line is exactly `Target skill: ${prefix}…`, and the test also asserts no lone high surrogate remains.
- **What was not tested:** No external service is involved in this path. The proof does not drive the browser UI; it verifies the exported approval policy result that supplies the UI/runtime approval description.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Review findings addressed
No maintainer review findings exist for this new follow-up branch. Pre-submit checks covered the follow-up risks: latest main still has the raw slice gap, no same-point open PR was found, and the regression crosses the persisted proposal and exported approval resolver path.

## Regression Test Plan
- **Target test file:** `src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** A pending proposal is created with a target skill name shaped as `"n".repeat(availableSkillNameLength - 2) + "\u{1F600}tail"`, causing the old truncation limit to land inside the emoji surrogate pair.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The test reaches the approval description through real proposal creation and the exported resolver, while keeping the assertion focused on the one bounded display field that had the raw slice.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts
git show origin/main:src/skills/workshop/policy.ts | grep -n "requestedSkillName\.slice(0, Math.max(0, availableSkillNameLength - 1))"
```

## Risk / Compatibility
Existing approval text remains bounded to the same maximum and still appends the same ellipsis for long target names. The only observable change is that truncation will not split a surrogate pair; the displayed target name may be one UTF-16 code unit shorter when the limit lands inside an astral character.

## What was not changed
- **What did NOT change:** Does not change Skill Workshop approval policy, lifecycle action selection, timeout behavior, allowed decisions, proposal lookup, proposal schema, proposal persistence, skill apply/reject/quarantine behavior, control-character sanitization, or approval description max length.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** Source-of-truth boundary: `buildLifecycleApprovalDescription` is the canonical formatter that constructs `requireApproval.description` for lifecycle tool approvals. This patch fixes that formatter before the approval request is returned, rather than post-processing a UI mirror, log copy, or test-only representation.

## Root Cause
- **Root cause:** Root cause is the source formatter `buildLifecycleApprovalDescription` shortening `requestedSkillName` with raw JavaScript `slice`. Because JavaScript string indices are UTF-16 code units, slicing at the computed approval boundary can cut between the high and low surrogate of an emoji or another astral code point.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The patch replaces the raw code-unit slice at the single target-name formatter with the shared UTF-16-safe truncation helper. Every lifecycle approval description with an overlong target skill name flows through this formatter, so the invalid-surrogate source is removed before the approval payload is returned.
